#### References to other Issues or PRs

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

Issue found while investigating [report](https://groups.google.com/g/sympy/c/FJt8rP8XTDM) on mailing list where apparently `cse` was capturing a symbol as a replacement pattern. This can be reproduced by introducing an UnevaluatedExpr which rebuilds to a symbol; the root cause for doing the rebuild (which was intended *not* to happen) was a test involving a tuple and list container which compared as unequal (and thus permitted the rebuild).


#### Other comments


#### AI Generation Disclosure

Author noted issue and ChatGPT located the issue and suggested the correction and test which were added.

#### Release Notes


<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* simplify
  * an inadvertent rebuild of an UnevaluateExpr is now avoided
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->
diff:
diff --git a/sympy/simplify/cse_main.py b/sympy/simplify/cse_main.py
index 0541cfc5a3ea..aab21a6e80a2 100644
--- a/sympy/simplify/cse_main.py
+++ b/sympy/simplify/cse_main.py
@@ -694,7 +694,7 @@ def _rebuild(expr):
             args = expr.args
 
         new_args = list(map(_rebuild, args))
-        if isinstance(expr, Unevaluated) or new_args != args:
+        if isinstance(expr, Unevaluated) or new_args != list(args):
             new_expr = expr.func(*new_args)
         else:
             new_expr = expr
diff --git a/sympy/simplify/tests/test_cse.py b/sympy/simplify/tests/test_cse.py
index c111e607b2ae..6a22626017d4 100644
--- a/sympy/simplify/tests/test_cse.py
+++ b/sympy/simplify/tests/test_cse.py
@@ -558,6 +558,9 @@ def test_cse_unevaluated():
         msg = f'Expected common subexpression {xp1} or {-xp1}, instead got {ue}'
         assert False, msg
 
+    p = Pow(x, 1, evaluate=False)
+    assert cse([p, p]) == ([(x0, p)], [x0, x0])
+
 
 def test_cse__performance():
     nexprs, nterms = 3, 20

issue_comments.author: moorepants
issue_comments.body:
Here is the behavior in the latest release 1.14.0 (for reference):

```
In [8]: import sympy as sm

In [9]: x = sm.symbols('x')

In [10]: p = sm.Pow(x, 1, evaluate=False)

In [11]: p
Out[11]: x**1

In [12]: sm.cse([p, p])
Out[12]: ([(x0, x)], [x0, x0])
```

title: cse: use list(args) for comparison
